name: Wayward Weapons
summary: At the Valley of Trials, Gornek sends new recruits to recover weapons for the encampment. With young warriors arriving to serve the Horde, supplies run thin, and the weaponsmith needs old arms returned to use.

sections.title: Arming the New Blood
sections.body: New recruits face harsh trials in Durotar's red wastes. Many arrive ready to pledge their blades to the warchief, straining the encampment's weapon stocks. Weaponsmith Kzan Thornslash struggles to meet demand, especially when early lessons prove fatal or humiliating for the unready.

sections.title: A Test of Resourcefulness
sections.body: Overseer Gornek makes the shortage a practical trial. He sends fresh arrivals to recover abandoned blades and blunt training weapons left by recruits who fell or fled. Bring the recovered arms to Kzan, and he can repair and temper them for the next wave. New recruits learn that survival in the Horde calls for scavenging as well as swinging steel.

faq.q: Why are there so many abandoned training weapons lying around?
aliases: why are weapons on the ground
faq.answer: Some recruits lack the strength or resolve the Horde demands. Careless or frightened newcomers leave their gear behind, while others fall to local boars and scorpids, scattering their issued arms across the dirt.
Kzan Thornslash is the weaponsmith inside the Den in the Valley of Trials. He outfits new recruits, repairs battered training gear, and maintains the Horde's martial supplies in the starting valley.
Gornek, the overseer outside the Den, sends new recruits to help. He watches incoming aspirants, judges their basic potential, and assigns them immediate needs around the trial grounds.

faq.q: What will Kzan do with these salvaged weapons?
aliases: what happens to the training weapons
faq.answer: Kzan repairs, sharpens, and restores the battered practice weapons. With resources in Durotar sparse and recruits arriving constantly, salvaged iron and wood are reused to train the next wave.

faq.q: Where is this quest taking place?
faq.answer: You are in the Valley of Trials, an isolated canyon in southern Durotar where young orcs and Darkspear trolls begin their path as warriors for the Horde.

faq.q: Why doesn't the Horde just forge entirely new weapons?
faq.answer: Durotar is rugged and arid, with few easily reached iron deposits, and the young Horde cannot afford waste. Reusing practice blades from washouts saves raw metal for frontline troops.

angles.text: In Durotar, every scrap of metal counts. As a blacksmith, you help reclaim ruined gear and rework battered edges into tools of war.
As a warrior, you learn to respect your weapons. Recovering arms left by failed recruits calls for discipline and self-reliance before combat begins.
As a member of the Horde, you endure in Durotar through grit and resourcefulness, saving weapons even when those unfit to carry them cast them aside.
